solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rum, unusual in a sea rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the assembled letters are read from the bottom upwards
in places the word for unusual inside the letters for a sea

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
rare means unusual

explanation.surface: A sailor's tot of rum, something unusual out on a heaving sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' builds ARAREMED; 'rising' turns it upside down in the column. 'Rum' looks like the old adjective for odd but names the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a dark rum from Guyana, named after the river and region there.

clue.text: Flipping extremely cold bird

indicators.note: flipping reads like a mild curse, but here it turns the letters over so they run upwards

parts.note: extremely means too, as in too hot
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: An exasperated birdwatcher complaining that it's flipping freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a swear word; it turns TOO + C upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The coot is a black waterbird with a white forehead shield, found on ponds and lakes.

clue.text: Fine isn't commonly collected by vacant dogsbody

indicators.note: the outer letters gather up the colloquial word, so it sits between them
a vacant word has its insides emptied, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: ain't is the common, nonstandard form of isn't

explanation.surface: A sniffy remark that a menial worker with nothing in his head doesn't gather fine things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' empties dogsbody to D...Y; 'collected by' puts AINT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dainty and fine both describe something delicate, small and exquisitely made.

clue.text: Court page more courteous being raised by court

indicators.note: in a down clue, being raised means the word is read upwards

parts.note: nicer means more polite or courteous
CT is the abbreviation for court, as in street names

explanation.surface: A courtier's page, more polite than most, being promoted by the royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being raised' turns NICER upwards to RECIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A precinct is an enclosed space around a building, much like a court or courtyard.

clue.text: Betrothal half finishes man purchasing a diamond?

indicators.note: half asks for just the first two of the four letters of the synonym

parts.note: finishes means ends

indicators.note: a man purchasing something holds it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a man
a diamond is an example of a gem, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A betrothal half over by the time the man buys a diamond ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the front two letters of the synonym; 'purchasing' means the man holds A plus the stone. The question mark flags diamond as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement is a formal promise to marry, which is exactly what a betrothal is.

clue.text: Stripped off for the audience and produced claps

indicators.note: for the audience means as heard by listeners, so the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: peeled, as of skin or clothing, means stripped off

explanation.surface: A striptease performer who took it all off for the audience and drew applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claps' looks like applause but means claps of thunder or bells ringing out.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells or thunder that rang out loudly made peals, which are resounding claps of sound.

clue.text: Carefree young woman coming out gay

parts.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman coming out into society
in its old sense of joyful, gay matches walking on air

explanation.surface: A light-hearted debutante announcing her sexuality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' means a debutante's first season, and 'gay' its old sense of elated, as in walking on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes someone confident, charming and untroubled, so carefree in manner.

clue.text: Flog and tie up heartlessly in protest

indicators.note: in puts the reversed short word inside the word for protest

parts.note: to rail is to protest angrily

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read upwards
heartlessly removes the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone tied up in a protest, perhaps being flogged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes the middle I out of TIE to give TE; 'up' turns it to ET, put 'in' RAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog something is colloquially to sell it, and retail means to sell goods to the public.

clue.text: Offends having right to start rows

indicators.note: to start means the letter is moved from its place to the front of the word

parts.note: angers means offends

explanation.surface: Someone who offends others, being entitled to start rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' moves the R of ANGERS to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranges are lines or rows of things, as in a range of hills or of cupboards.

clue.text: Dodgy tendency

definitions.meaning: slang for crooked or corrupt, as of a policeman
a natural inclination or aptitude for something

explanation.surface: A dubious inclination.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is slang for dishonest, and as a noun it means a natural leaning or talent.

clue.text: Unequipped to cross frozen water plain

indicators.note: to cross means the first word stretches across the second, holding it inside

parts.note: not able means unequipped to do something
ice is frozen water

explanation.surface: Someone lacking the gear to walk across a frozen plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like a landscape on the ice; it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain is clearly visible or obvious, so it is easily seen.

clue.text: Waterlogged pitch following crowd's return

indicators.note: following sends the throwing word after the reversed crowd word
return means the word for crowd is turned back on itself

parts.note: to ram is to crowd or press in
to shy is to pitch or throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A sodden football pitch after the crowd comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a sports field but is a verb meaning to throw, as at a coconut shy, a British fairground stall.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy ground is soft and wet like a marsh, so saturated with water.

clue.text: Socialist rabble nagging starts and ends next rally

indicators.note: starts and ends picks the first and last letters of each of the three words before it

parts.note: then means next, as in and then

explanation.surface: A left-wing mob heckling at the start and finish of the next political rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts and ends' takes S..T, R..E and N..G from the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally troops or a team is to restore their spirit, making them stronger.

clue.text: Slur from boozer, free to embrace sweetheart

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub, and an inn is a pub

indicators.note: to embrace means the word for free wraps around the letter

parts.note: to undo a knot is to free it
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: An insult hurled in a pub, from someone free to hug their sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' here is the heart of 'sweet', its middle letter E, which UNDO embraces.
explanation.definitionFit: An insinuation is an indirect slight on someone's character, so a kind of slur.

clue.text: One sails Channel around Portsmouth — it's brisk

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is one who sails

indicators.note: around means the word for channel goes round the letter

parts.note: a rut is a channel or groove
the mouth of the word Port is its first letter, P

explanation.surface: A sailor crossing the English Channel near the naval port of Portsmouth on a brisk day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' looks like the English Channel but means RUT; 'Portsmouth' is the mouth, first letter, of Port. Portsmouth is England's naval port.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisk and abrupt both describe a short, curt manner of speaking.

clue.text: Flower border in expert's estimation's top

indicators.note: in puts the word for border inside the expert's letters

parts.note: a pro is an expert, so expert's gives the plural-looking pro's
a rim is an edge or border

indicators.note: top, in a down clue, picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gardener praising a flower border as the best, in an expert's view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' looks like a flower bed but means RIM, set 'in' PROS.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring wildflower common in British hedgerows.

clue.text: Capital of America following that dollar, half-done

parts.note: then means following that, as in and then
the dollar sign is an S with a stroke through it; take away the stroke and only the S is left

explanation.surface: A capital of America, following a slump in the dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of America' tempts a US city, but 'Capital' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece.

clue.text: Growth of flowers well in garden

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: The growth of flowers that do well in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'flowerS WELL IN Garden'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump or bump on the body is a growth, such as a tumour or swollen part.

clue.text: Farmer in Oz, penning sheep

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: An Australian farmer rounding up sheep into a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is held in 'farMER IN Oz'.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed of sheep, prized for fine wool, is farmed widely in Australia.

clue.text: Caught over middle, reportedly, for match

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is replaced by one that sounds like it

parts.note: the inside of something is its middle

explanation.surface: A cricket report: caught after an over in the middle of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that coincide correspond or agree exactly, so they match.

clue.text: Kind of sauce for duck, poured say, over

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, hence O
ran means poured or flowed

indicators.note: over means the short abbreviation is turned over, read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: eg (for example) means say

explanation.surface: A recipe for duck with its sauce poured over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the dish but is the cricket nought, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Duck a l'orange is the classic dish served with this citrus sauce.

clue.text: Sweat slightly, changing hands at first

indicators.note: the right hand at the front becomes the left, so the opening R becomes L

parts.note: rather means slightly, as in rather cold

explanation.surface: Someone sweating a little as they swap hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse in a lather is covered in frothy sweat, so the noun means sweat.

clue.text: Start to land on snake here? No

definitions.text: Start to land on snake here? No

indicators.note: on means the letter sits on top of the snake in this down clue
start to picks out the first letter of the next word

parts.note: an adder is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A player in Snakes and Ladders asking whether to land on a snake square.
explanation.walkthrough: In Snakes and Ladders, landing on a snake sends you down; landing at the foot of this sends you up, hence 'No'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the board game you climb up these when you land, the opposite of sliding down a snake.

clue.text: Genius of Obama's term in disarray

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is drawn from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A jibe that the genius of the Obama presidency fell into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disarray' looks like an anagram signal but is just part of the hiding place: obaMA'S TERM IN Disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant planner or intellect is called a mastermind, so a genius.

clue.text: Spymaster's expression of approval for spy

parts.note: M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories
ole is the Spanish cry of approval at a bullfight

explanation.surface: A spy chief's nod of approval for an agent.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent planted inside an organisation to pass on its secrets is a spy.

clue.text: Setter perhaps tense with stomach turning

indicators.note: turning means the combined letters are turned round, read upwards here

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
tum is a colloquial word for stomach

explanation.surface: The crossword setter feels tense, with a churning stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the puzzle's compiler but is a breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a dog breed, and a mongrel dog of any kind is a mutt.

clue.text: They turn back with gutless lecherous looks

definitions.text: They turn back with gutless lecherous looks

indicators.note: back means the short word for a turn is read backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

indicators.note: gutless removes the middle letter, the guts, of the word

parts.note: leers are lecherous looks

explanation.surface: Men who turn round to leer at passers-by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' removes the middle E; 'back' turns the game word round. The whole clue also describes such men, so it is a semi-&lit.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes people who look round to eye others lustfully.

clue.text: Public individual giving hint

parts.note: overt means open or public
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A public figure dropping a hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle suggestion or implied meaning carried alongside the main one is a hint.
